extra_misconceptions.fact: The requirement measures your combined grade average across all classes taken during that full grading term or semester.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Earning a B or higher in just one favorite subject satisfies the requirement for an overall term average of 80 percent.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Option 1b allows any Scout to qualify by demonstrating measurable grade improvement over the immediately preceding term.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Students who earned lower than a B average cannot earn the Scholarship merit badge until they reach an 80 percent GPA.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scouts must present official report cards or transcripts from two consecutive terms to verify improvement or a B average.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An unverified verbal report or a screenshot of a single quiz score is sufficient proof of your semester grade average.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Grade averages or improvements must cover a complete official school term, quarter, trimester, or semester to count.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Improving grades on a two-week progress check fulfills the requirement without finishing the full grading period first.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your overall term GPA when a high-credit core course drops by one letter grade compared to an elective?

What calculation confirms that your combined numerical scores across all classes meet or exceed the 80 percent average?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Requirement 2b explicitly excludes teachers and other professionals employed at your school from the two career interviews.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Interviewing your favorite classroom teacher or high school guidance counselor fulfills the career interview requirement.

extra_misconceptions.fact: You must demonstrate active use of a daily planner showing real assignments, scheduled activities, and time management.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Showing a blank calendar app or a freshly purchased paper planner satisfies the daily assignment tracking requirement.

extra_misconceptions.fact: You must compile a list of local educational places, visit one, and report specifically on how you educated yourself there.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Visiting a local museum on a family outing counts automatically without reporting how you used the site for self-education.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Online sources often lack editorial review, so researchers must weigh internet speed against verified library periodicals.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Internet search engines replace print books and library periodicals because online sources are always more current and true.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it necessary to secure approval from both your counselor and parent before contacting professionals for interviews?
Under what condition does a professional working at your school fail to qualify as an interviewee for Requirement 2b?
What scheduling entries in your daily planner prove that you track long-term project milestones alongside daily homework?
Which evaluation criteria help you verify whether an internet article is as reliable as a peer-reviewed library periodical?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The note must come directly from the school principal or from another school official specifically named by the principal.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any classroom teacher or athletic coach can sign the school citizenship note without authorization from the principal.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The official note must explicitly confirm that your behavior, leadership, and service over the past year were satisfactory.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A school attendance printout showing zero disciplinary suspensions is enough to satisfy the principal's note requirement.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Home-schooled Scouts must still fulfill Requirement 3 by obtaining the signed certification note from a parent counterpart.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Home-schooled Scouts are exempt from Requirement 3 because their educational environment does not have a school principal.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The written certification must cover your conduct, leadership, and service across the entire preceding twelve-month year.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Good behavior during a single week of classes is sufficient for the school principal to certify your citizenship record.

extra_socratic_questions: Which three specific areas of school citizenship must the principal or designated official verify in your written note?
Who is authorized to sign your citizenship note if your school principal delegates that task to another staff member?
What time period must the school official evaluate when certifying that your behavior, leadership, and service were good?
Where should a home-schooled Scout obtain official verification of satisfactory behavior, leadership, and service?

extra_misconceptions.fact: You must show active participation in the extracurricular activity and explain what you learned about teamwork and benefits.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Signing up on a school club roster at the start of the year fulfills Requirement 4a without attending meetings or events.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Option 4b requires collaborative participation in a team school project from the past semester and your team contributions.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Completing a solo extra-credit research paper counts for Option 4b as long as you present it in front of your classmates.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Extracurricular activities for Option 4a must be sponsored by or connected to your school rather than outside organizations.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scouting troop campouts or municipal recreation sports leagues qualify as extracurricular school activities for Option 4a.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Effective teamwork requires sharing responsibilities, communicating with peers, and making positive contributions to the group.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Doing all the work yourself on a group assignment is the best way to demonstrate teamwork to your merit badge counselor.

extra_socratic_questions: What specific evidence shows your counselor that you actively participated in an extracurricular school club or team?
Which personal actions during a semester group project demonstrate a positive contribution rather than passive attendance?
What happens to a school project team when one member takes over every task instead of dividing duties by skill?
Under what condition does an outside community youth league fail to count as an extracurricular school activity?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Requirement 5 specifically mandates a written report of 250 to 300 words rather than an informal oral discussion.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Giving a five-minute spoken talk to your counselor can substitute for writing the 250-to-300-word essay in Requirement 5.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Your report must contain between 250 and 300 words and cover all required prompts for either Option 5a or Option 5b.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Writing a short 100-word paragraph is acceptable for Requirement 5 as long as it mentions your favorite future career.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Option 5b requires discussing two distinct careers of interest and explaining how specific school classes support both.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Option 5b only asks you to describe one dream job and the college degree required to enter that specific profession.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Option 5a requires explaining both how current schooling helps your future and how you will continue self-education later.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Option 5a is complete once you explain how current school classes help you graduate and get into a four-year university.

extra_socratic_questions: What word-count range must your written report fall within to satisfy the length specification for Requirement 5?
